output.name: Hanor
output.myth: When Aun cut the string he did not cut it clean, and the sky went up so fast that Sil had to run after it along the tide. He tied a stone to the last of the line, so he would know how far the sky had fallen from the islands. Hesk saw and kept count on her reel. That stone is Hanor. It swings in the Leeward dark from a bar of bone, and each night it hangs a little straighter. Low in the south, the Upturned Hull lies keel-up, her lamps still lit. Up in the north-west the Knot That Would Not Loose holds fast, where Tavo blew until the spray stood like walls. When Hanor hangs plumb, the sky will stand and come home. Tavo tries to knock it sideways for sport. Then the sailors feel the sea move under them and fall to their knees. Mind your own line, the grandmothers say. Tie a stone to what you fear losing, so you know where it went.
output.finding: From the Upturned Hull, low in the south, look a fist and a half, a little under a hand-span, straight north up the sky to find Hanor.
